\"\"\n$inAssistantBlock = $false\n\nforeach ($line in $lines) {\n    $trimmed = $line.Trim()\n    \n    # Detect role markers (JSONL format)\n    if ($trimmed -match '\"role\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"') {\n        # Save previous block if it was assistant\n        if ($inAssistantBlock -and $currentBlock.Trim().Length -gt 10) {\n            $turnSeq++\n            $text = $currentBlock.Trim()\n            $isBlueprint = ($text -match '```|`````|fenced code block|\\b(SPEC|SPECIFICATION|BLUEPRINT|ARCHITECTURE|SCHEMA|DESIGN)\\b' -and $text.Length -gt 200)\n            $dnaRecords += [ordered]@{\n                run    = $run\n                seq    = $turnSeq\n                type   = if ($isBlueprint) { \"blueprint\" } else { \"prose\" }\n                chars  = $text.Length\n                text   = $text\n            }\n        }\n        $currentRole = $matches[1]\n        $currentBlock = \"\"\n        $inAssistantBlock = ($currentRole -eq \"assistant\")\n    }\n    # Detect plain-text speaker markers\n    elseif ($trimmed -match '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]') {\n        if ($inAssistantBlock -and $currentBlock.Trim().Length -gt 10) {\n            $turnSeq++\n            $text = $currentBlock.Trim()\n            $isBlueprint = ($text -match '```|`````|fenced code block|\\b(SPEC|SPECIFICATION|BLUEPRINT|ARCHITECTURE|SCHEMA|DESIGN)\\b' -and $text.Length -gt 200)\n            $dnaRecords += [ordered]@{\n                run    = $run\n                seq    = $turnSeq\n                type   = if ($isBlueprint) { \"blueprint\" } else { \"prose\" }\n                chars  = $text.Length\n                text   = $text\n            }\n        }\n        $inAssistantBlock = $true\n        $currentBlock = $trimmed -replace '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]\\s*', ''\n    }\n    # Accumulate lines within a block\n    elseif ($inAssistantBlock) {\n        $currentBlock += \"`n$line\"\n    }\n}\n\n# Flush final block\nif ($inAssistantBlock -and $currentBlock.Trim().Length -gt 10) {\n    $turnSeq++\n    $text = $currentBlock.Trim()\n    $isBlueprint = ($text -match '```|`````|fenced code block|\\b(SPEC|SPECIFICATION|BLUEPRINT|ARCHITECTURE|SCHEMA|DESIGN)\\b' -and $text.Length -gt 200)\n    $dnaRecords += [ordered]@{\n        run    = $run\n        seq    = $turnSeq\n        type   = if ($isBlueprint) { \"blueprint\" } else { \"prose\" }\n        chars  = $text.Length\n        text   = $text\n    }\n}\n\n# ═══════════════════════════════════════════\n# EC-026: DUAL-HASH DETERMINISM NORMALIZATION\n# ═══════════════════════════════════════════\n# DISCREPANCY DOCUMENTED:\n#   JSONL path (line ~190): role-marker line (\"role\":\"assistant\") is EXCLUDED from $currentBlock\n#   Plain-text path (line ~209): speaker-marker line (\"AGENT:\") is INCLUDED with prefix stripped\n#   Result: same semantic turn produces different character counts depending on which parser path was taken.\n# FIX: Normalize both paths — strip role-marker and speaker-prefix lines to empty before accumulation.\n#   After normalization, both paths should produce identical byte counts for the same semantic content.\n$dnaTotalCharsJsonl  = 0\n$dnaTotalCharsPlain  = 0\n$dnaJsonlRecords     = ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.text -notmatch '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]' }).Count\n$dnaPlainRecords     = $dnaRecords.Count - $dnaJsonlRecords\nif ($dnaJsonlRecords -gt 0 -and $dnaPlainRecords -gt 0) {\n    $dnaTotalCharsJsonl = ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.text -notmatch '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]' } | Measure-Object -Property chars -Sum).Sum\n    $dnaTotalCharsPlain = ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.text -match '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]' } | Measure-Object -Property chars -Sum).Sum\n}\nif ($dnaTotalCharsJsonl -gt 0 -and $dnaTotalCharsPlain -gt 0) {\n    $charDiff = [Math]::Abs($dnaTotalCharsJsonl - $dnaTotalCharsPlain)\n    $avgChars = ($dnaTotalCharsJsonl + $dnaTotalCharsPlain) / 2\n    if ($avgChars -gt 0) {\n        $pctDiff = ($charDiff / $avgChars) * 100\n        if ($pctDiff -gt 1.0) {\n            Write-Warning \"EC-026 DUAL-HASH DRIFT: JSONL-path chars=$dnaTotalCharsJsonl vs plain-path chars=$dnaTotalCharsPlain — diff $pctDiff% (>1%). DNA hash may not be deterministic across parser paths.\"\n        } else {\n            Write-Host \"  EC-026 OK: JSONL/plain char diff = $pctDiff% (within 1% tolerance)\"\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n$dnaCount = $dnaRecords.Count\n$dnaBlueprintCount = ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.type -eq \"blueprint\" }).Count\n\nif ($dnaCount -gt 0) {\n    $dnaPath = \"$dnaDir\\dna-run$run.json\"\n    $dnaRecords | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content $dnaPath -Encoding UTF8\n    Write-Host \"STAGE 3 ✓ DNA: $dnaCount records ($dnaBlueprintCount blueprints) → $dnaPath\"\n} else {\n    Write-Warning \"STAGE 3 ⚠ DNA_GAP — 0 assistant turns extracted from RRL\"\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 4 — LEDGER (MERKLE — DUAL HASH OVER SOUL + DNA)\n\n```powershell\n# --- Helper Functions ---\nfunction Get-Next-LedgerID {\n    param([string]$LedgerDir)\n    $existing = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $LedgerDir -Filter \"HL-*.json\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |\n        ForEach-Object { if ($_.Name -match 'HL-(\\d+)\\.json$') { [int]$matches[1] } }\n    if ($existing) { return ($existing | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum + 1 }\n    return 1\n}\nfunction Get-Tail-Ledger-Hash {\n    param([string]$LedgerDir)\n    $latest = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $LedgerDir -Filter \"HL-*.json\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |\n        Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 1\n    if (-not $latest) { return $null }\n    $entry = Get-Content $latest.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json\n    return $entry.merkle_hash\n}\nfunction Compute-Sha256 {\n    param([string]$InputString)\n    $bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($InputString)\n    $hash  = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create().ComputeHash($bytes)\n    return [System.BitConverter]::ToString($hash) -replace '-', ''\n}\n\nif (-not (Test-Path $ledgerDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ledgerDir -Force | Out-Null }\n\n$nextHL     = Get-Next-LedgerID -LedgerDir $ledgerDir\n$parentHash = Get-Tail-Ledger-Hash -LedgerDir $ledgerDir\n\n$timestamp = (Get-Date -Format 'o')\n\n# Dual hash: soul_hash (user words) + dna_hash (agent words)\n$soulHash = Compute-Sha256 $rrlText\n$dnaHash  = if ($dnaCount -gt 0) { Compute-Sha256 ($dnaRecords | ConvertTo-Json -Compress) } else { \"DNA_GAP\" }\n\n$ledgerHash = Compute-Sha256 \"$soulHash|$dnaHash|$parentHash|$timestamp\"\n\n$ledgerEntry = [ordered]@{\n    hl_id          = \"HL-$nextHL\"\n    session_id     = \"sov100-roman-run$run\"\n    rrl_source     = $rrlPath\n    char_count     = $rrlChars\n    byte_count     = $rrlBytes\n    soul_hash      = $soulHash\n    dna_hash       = $dnaHash\n    dna_blueprint_count = $dnaBlueprintCount\n    merkle_parent  = $parentHash\n    merkle_hash    = $ledgerHash\n    sealed_at      = $timestamp\n    sov100         = $true\n    run            = $run\n}\n\n$ledgerPath = \"$ledgerDir\\HL-$nextHL.json\"\n$ledgerEntry | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content $ledgerPath -Encoding UTF8\nWrite-Host \"STAGE 4 ✓ LEDGER: HL-$nextHL → parent HL-$($nextHL-1) | soul_hash=$($soulHash.Substring(0,16))... | dna_hash=$($dnaHash.Substring(0,16))...\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 5 — STARMAP (POINTER MAP — ANTI-BLOAT)\n\n```powershell\nif (-not (Test-Path $starmapDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $starmapDir -Force | Out-Null }\n\n$soulTurnIds = if ($dnaCount -gt 0) { \n    ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.type -eq \"prose\" } | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { \"turn-$($_.seq)\" }) -join \",\"\n} else { \"\" }\n\n$dnaTurnIds = if ($dnaCount -gt 0) {\n    ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.type -eq \"blueprint\" } | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { \"seq-$($_.seq)\" }) -join \",\"\n} else { \"\" }\n\n$blueprintLocations = if ($dnaCount -gt 0) {\n    ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.type -eq \"blueprint\" } | ForEach-Object { \"dna-run$run.json:seq-$($_.seq)\" }) -join \"; \"\n} else { \"\" }\n\n$starmap = [ordered]@{\n    run                  = $run\n    rrl_path             = $rrlPath\n    ledger_id            = \"HL-$nextHL\"\n    soul_turn_ids        = $soulTurnIds\n    dna_turn_ids         = $dnaTurnIds\n    blueprint_locations  = $blueprintLocations\n    char_count           = $rrlChars\n    merkle_hash          = $ledgerHash\n    created_at           = $timestamp\n} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4\n\n$starmapPath = \"$starmapDir\\starmap-run$runPad.json\"\n$starmap | Set-Content $starmapPath -Encoding UTF8\nWrite-Host \"STAGE 5 ✓ STARMAP: $starmapPath (pointer map, not content dump)\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 6 — SOULKEYS (KEYWORD INDEX — SOUL + DNA, READ-MERGE-WRITE)\n\nExtract keywords over BOTH SOUL (user words) AND DNA (agent blueprints).\nNever `-Append` on JSON. Always read → merge in memory → overwrite.\n\n```powershell\nif (-not (Test-Path $keywordDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $keywordDir -Force | Out-Null }\n\n# Extract terms from both SOUL (RRL user text) and DNA (agent text + blueprints)\n$combinedText = $rrlText\nif ($dnaCount -gt 0) {\n    $combinedText += \"`n\" + ($dnaRecords | ForEach-Object { $_.text }) -join \"`n\"\n}\n\n$words = $combinedText -split '\\s+' | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 4 } | \n         Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^(this|that|with|from|have|been|were|they|will|would|could|should|about|there|their|which|what|when|make|like|just|some|more|than|also|very|much|many|into|over|been|being|through|where|after|before|because|being|against|between|without|within|along|follow|coming|think|know|take|come|make|look|want|give|work|time|year|good|some|them|would|could|other|about|which|their|there|first|would|these|those|under|should|after|where|since|still|every|being|great|where|place|found|sound|below|seen|enough|while|both|show|those|taken|might|long|down|part|same|back|call|hand|high|last|next|left|turn|move|live|believe|happen|bring|write|provide|sit|stand|lose|pay|meet|include|continue|set|learn|change|lead|understand|watch|follow|stop|create|speak|read|allow|add|spend|grow|open|walk|win|offer|remember|love|consider|appear|buy|wait|serve|die|send|expect|build|stay|fall|cut|reach|kill|remain|suggest|raise|pass|sell|require|report|decide|pull|develop|return|explain|hope|describe|decide|share|provide|cover|fall|catch|draw|choose|wish|teach|test|wear|supply|shut|hold|push|close|deal|fill|break|support|record|cut|heat|watch|raise|reach|fly|land|cancel|graduate|enroll|register|complete|submit|assign|grade|assess|evaluate|review|approve|reject|confirm|notify|alert|remind|schedule|book|reserve|request|order|purchase|pay|charge|refund|invoice|receipt|transaction|payment|deposit|withdraw|transfer|balance|account|statement|ledger|audit|compliance|regulation|policy|contract|agreement|terms|conditions|liability|warranty|dispute|resolution|arbitration|mediation|escalate|appeal|petition|claim|evidence|document|certificate|attest|verify|validate|authenticate|authorize|authenticate|deprecate|obsolete|retire|decommission|archive|purge|delete|destroy|shred|encrypt|decrypt|cipher|hash|salt|key|cert|token|session|cookie|cache|queue|buffer|stream|socket|pipe|channel|bandwidth|latency|throughput|capacity|quota|limit|threshold|rate|pace|burst|flow|routing|dispatch|deliver|notify|trigger|fire|emit|broadcast }\n$wordFreq = $words | Group-Object | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 30\n\n$rfkwPath = \"$keywordDir\\rfkw-run$runPad.txt\"\n$wordFreq | ForEach-Object { \"$($_.Count) | $($_.Name)\" } | Set-Content $rfkwPath -Encoding UTF8\n\n# Update inverted index: READ → MERGE → WRITE (NO APPEND)\n$inverted = if (Test-Path $idxPath) {\n    (Get-Content $idxPath -Raw) | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable\n} else {\n    @{}\n}\n\nforeach ($kw in $wordFreq) {\n    $term = $kw.Name.Trim().ToLower()\n    $weight = [int]$kw.Count\n    if (-not $inverted[$term]) {\n        $inverted[$term] = @()\n    }\n    $entry = @{ run=$run; category=\"soul+key\"; weight=$weight }\n    $already = $false\n    foreach ($e in $inverted[$term]) {\n        if ($e.run -eq $run) { $already = $true; break }\n    }\n    if (-not $already) {\n        # EC-027: COLLISION HANDLER — prevents serialization failure on ConvertTo-Json\n        # When ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable deserializes a single-element array, it may\n        # produce a scalar instead of a collection. += on a scalar corrupts the structure.\n        if ($inverted.ContainsKey($term)) {\n            $existing = $inverted[$term]\n            if ($existing -is [System.Collections.ICollection]) {\n                $existing += $entry\n            } else {\n                $inverted[$term] = @($existing; $entry)\n            }\n        } else {\n            $inverted[$term] = $entry\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n$inverted | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content $idxPath -Encoding UTF8\nWrite-Host \"STAGE 6 ✓ SOULKEYS: $($inverted.Count) terms in index | $rfkwPath\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 7 — S2Pipeline (EXECUTION ARTIFACT + VERIFICATION)\n\nOne command runs RRL→SOULKEYS in order, writes the result record, and does not report COMPLETE unless every stage verifies REAL.\n\n```powershell\n# Registry vars (defined here, consumed by STAGE 8 as well)\n$artRegistryDir = \"$repo\\CANON\\ART-REGISTRY\"\n$syncedPieces   = @()\n$rrlFidelity    = if ($hasUser -and $hasAssistant) { \"REAL\" } else { \"HOLLOW\" }\n\n$s2Record = [ordered]@{\n    run_number        = $run\n    executed_at       = (Get-Date -Format 'o')\n    head_sha          = (git rev-parse --short HEAD)\n    rrl_path          = $rrlPath\n    rrl_chars         = $rrlChars\n    rrl_bytes         = $rrlBytes\n    rrl_fidelity      = if ($hasUser -and $hasAssistant) { \"REAL\" } else { \"HOLLOW\" }\n    session_id        = \"sov100-roman-run$run\"\n    soul_event_id     = if ($receipt) { $receipt.event_id } else { \"SOUL_GAP\" }\n    soulcount         = if ($receipt -and $receipt.count_after) { $receipt.count_after } else { 0 }\n    soul_level        = if ($receipt) { $receipt.level } else { \"UNKNOWN\" }\n    soul_count_before = if ($receipt) { $receipt.count_before } else { 0 }\n    soul_delta        = if ($receipt) { $receipt.delta } else { 0 }\n    dna_count         = $dnaCount\n    dna_blueprint_count = $dnaBlueprintCount\n    dna_status        = if ($dnaCount -gt 0) { if ($dnaBlueprintCount -gt 0) { \"REAL\" } else { \"HOLLOW\" } } else { \"MISSING\" }\n    ledger_id         = \"HL-$nextHL\"\n    starmap_file      = $starmapPath\n    keyword_file      = $rfkwPath\n    keyword_index     = $idxPath\n    s2pipeline_file   = $s2Path\n    registry_file     = if (Test-Path \"$artRegistryDir\\art-sync-run$runPad.json\") { \"$artRegistryDir\\art-sync-run$runPad.json\" } else { \"REGISTRY_SYNC_GAP\" }\n    registry_synced   = $syncedPieces.Count\n    result            = if ($rrlFidelity -eq \"REAL\" -and $dnaBlueprintCount -gt 0) { \"COMPLETE\" } else { \"GAP\" }\n}\n\n$s2Record | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content $s2Path -Encoding UTF8\nWrite-Host \"STAGE 7 ✓ S2Pipeline: $s2Path | result=$($s2Record.result)\"\n```\n\n**GATE:** Pipeline reports COMPLETE only when RRL is REAL (both speakers) AND DNA is REAL (assistant turns extracted). Any HOLLOW stage = GAP.\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 8 — REGISTRY SYNC (ART ARSENAL × SOULKEYS × STARMAP × LEDGER)\n\nCross-references this run's SOULKEYS against the art-arsenal registry.\nAny piece whose tags intersect the run's top keywords gets tagged with the run, HL ID, starmap pointer, and merkle hash.\nWrites a canonical artifact. Auto-fires every death — no human trigger needed.\n\n```powershell\nif (-not (Test-Path $artRegistryDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $artRegistryDir -Force | Out-Null }\n\n# 1. Pull this run's keywords from the SOULKEYS stage\n$runKeywords = @()\nif (Test-Path $rfkwPath) {\n    $runKeywords = (Get-Content $rfkwPath -Raw) -split \"`n\" |\n        Where-Object { $_ -match '^\\d+\\s*\\|' } |\n        ForEach-Object { (($_ -split '\\|')[1]).Trim().ToLower() } |\n        Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 2 }\n}\n\n# 2. Pull the full registry\n$regPieces = @()\ntry {\n    $regResp = Invoke-RestMethod \"https://phoenix-architecti.mrmichaelhobbs123.workers.dev/api/art?limit=400\" -TimeoutSec 15\n    $regPieces = $regResp.pieces\n} catch { Write-Warning \"REGISTRY_SYNC: registry fetch failed — $($_.Exception.Message)\" }\n\n# 3. For each piece: check keyword intersection + direct title mention in RRL\n$merkleShort  = if ($ledgerHash) { $ledgerHash.Substring(0,16) } else { \"LEDGER_GAP\" }\n\n$artSyncGap = $false\nforeach ($piece in $regPieces) {\n    if (-not $piece) { continue }\n    $pieceTags   = ($piece.tags -split ',') | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim().ToLower() } | Where-Object { $_ }\n    $pieceTitle  = ($piece.title -replace '[^a-zA-Z0-9 ]','').ToLower()\n    $matched     = @($pieceTags | Where-Object { $runKeywords -contains $_ })\n    $titleHit    = ($rrlText -match [regex]::Escape($piece.title)) -or ($rrlText -match [regex]::Escape($piece.url -replace '-hd\\.png|\\.png|isolated/',''))\n    if ($matched.Count -eq 0 -and -not $titleHit) { continue }\n\n    # Build notes tag preserving any existing notes\n    $existingNotes = if ($piece.notes) { $piece.notes } else { \"\" }\n    $runTag   = \"run$runPad\"\n    if ($existingNotes -notmatch $runTag) {\n        $appendNote = \"[$runTag | HL-$nextHL | $merkleShort | kw:$($matched -join ',') | sm:starmap-run$runPad.json]\"\n        $newNotes   = ($existingNotes + \" \" + $appendNote).Trim()\n        try {\n            $patchBody = @{ notes = $newNotes } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress\n            Invoke-RestMethod \"https://phoenix-architecti.mrmichaelhobbs123.workers.dev/api/art/$($piece.id)\" `\n                -Method PATCH -Body $patchBody -ContentType \"application/json\" -TimeoutSec 10 | Out-Null\n            $syncedPieces += [ordered]@{\n                id       = $piece.id\n                title    = $piece.title\n                url      = $piece.url\n                keywords = $matched\n                title_hit = $titleHit\n            }\n        } catch { $artSyncGap = $true; Write-Warning \"  PATCH failed for $($piece.title): $($_.Exception.Message)\" }\n    }\n}\nif ($artSyncGap) { Write-Host \"  ⚠ REGISTRY_SYNC_GAP — one or more PATCH calls failed; see seal §14\" }\n\n# 4. Write canonical artifact\n$artSyncPath = \"$artRegistryDir\\art-sync-run$runPad.json\"\n[ordered]@{\n    run           = $run\n    ledger_id     = \"HL-$nextHL\"\n    merkle_short  = $merkleShort\n    starmap_file  = \"starmap-run$runPad.json\"\n    keywords_file = \"rfkw-run$run.txt\"\n    keywords_used = $runKeywords\n    pieces_synced = $syncedPieces.Count\n    pieces        = $syncedPieces\n    executed_at   = $timestamp\n} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content $artSyncPath -Encoding UTF8\n\nWrite-Host \"STAGE 8 ✓ REGISTRY SYNC: $($syncedPieces.Count) pieces tagged → $artSyncPath | HL-$nextHL | keywords=$($runKeywords.Count)\"\n```\n\n**Connection law:** Every registry piece that matches a SOULKEY from this run carries the run, HL ID, merkle hash, and starmap pointer in its notes. This makes the art registry a living cross-reference — searchable by run, keyword, ledger entry, or starmap pointer.\n\n**Gap policy:** REGISTRY_SYNC fails gracefully (write `ART_SYNC_GAP`, continue). Never blocks death.\n\n---\n\n## GAP POLICY\n\n| Stage | Irreplaceable? | Failure Action |\n|-------|----------------|----------------|\n| RRL | **YES** | HALT — exit 1. No RRL = no run. |\n| SOUL | No | Write `SOUL_GAP`, continue. Verify next RISE. |\n| DNA | No | Write `DNA_GAP`, continue. Source is always the RRL — back-fill next RISE. |\n| LEDGER | No | Write `LEDGER_GAP`, continue. |\n| STARMAP | No | Write `STARMAP_GAP`, continue. |\n| SOULKEYS | No | Write `SOULKEYS_GAP`, continue. |\n| S2Pipeline | No | Write `PIPELINE_GAP`, continue. |\n| REGISTRY SYNC | No | Write `ART_SYNC_GAP`, continue. |\n\n**RISE reads all gaps. RISE never auto-fixes — that is DEATH territory.**\n\n---\n\n## DEATH SEAL SCHEMA (§1–§13)\n\n| § | Name | Required Content |\n|---|------|------------------|\n| 1 | HEADER | run tag, datetime ICT, theme, signal density, HEAD pre-death |\n| 2 | RAW SOUL DNA | verbatim Michael quotes, labeled CRITICAL / IMPORTANT / CONTEXT |\n| 3 | SOUL RECEIPT | event_id, count_before, count_after, delta, level, posted_at |\n| 4 | DECISIONS | numbered, impact, canon file affected |\n| 5 | CORRECTIONS | wrong → root cause → fix → docs read |\n| 6 | NEW PRINCIPLES | |\n| 7 | EMOTIONAL SIGNAL | |\n| 8 | OPEN QUESTIONS | |\n| 9 | UNFINISHED ACTIONS | with exact git add commands |\n| 10 | SYSTEM DESIGN | |\n| 11 | ARTIFACTS | paths + SHAs for all 7 chain artifacts + registry sync + dnaREGISTRY digest |\n| 12 | STATE SNAPSHOT | HEAD, branch, dirty tree, soulcount (= §3 count_after), dna_blueprint_count |\n| 13 | FINGERPRINT | agent, run#, commit SHA, platform death test result |\n| 14 | ART REGISTRY SYNC | pieces_synced count, art-sync-run{N}.json path, top keywords matched |\n| 15 | REGISTRY | CANON/REGISTRY/dna-registry-run{N}.json path, entry count, stale flag |\n\n§12 soulcount MUST equal §3 `count_after`. {"parentUuid":"7bbc9e20-7bdf-4f79-b60e-b2a0eeed9075","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"D:\\OB-1-CANONICAL\\.kilo\\command\\netpet-observability.md","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"D:\\OB-1-CANONICAL\\.kilo\\command\\netpet-observability.md","content":"# /netpet-observability — OBI Production Observability + Resilience Blueprint\n\n**What this covers:** Everything that happens BETWEEN deploys. Runtime visibility, synthetic monitoring, structured logging, alerting, graceful degradation, KV performance. Zero overlap with `/netpet-preflight` (which covers pre-deploy gates).\n\n**The gap this closes:** Today we find out OBI is broken when Michael rages. There is no proactive signal. No student session telemetry. No structured error trail. No canary. No auto-recovery. Flying completely blind in production between manual test runs.\n\n**Doctrine:** \"If a student has a bad session and nobody logged it, it didn't happen until Michael found out the hard way.\"\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 1 — SYNTHETIC CANARY (the most important layer — catches the endpointing class without a deploy)\n\n**The failure it prevents:** The endpointing bug was not caused by our code changing. Deepgram changed their API under us. No pre-deploy gate catches that because we weren't deploying. A canary running every 5 minutes against live Deepgram would have fired the day they changed the spec.\n\n**What it does:** Reuses the existing `keep-warm-ping` scheduled Worker or a separate cron trigger. Every 5 minutes:\n1. Hits `/api/deepgram-token?studentId=sov100-test-magic` — asserts 200 + token\n2. Opens `wss://agent.deepgram.com/v1/agent/converse` with that token\n3. Sends the full Settings object\n4. Asserts `SettingsApplied` within 8s — **not** an Error\n5. Asserts at least one binary audio chunk within 5s after SettingsApplied\n6. Closes cleanly\n\n**Red state:** writes `canary:state = \"RED\"` + `canary:last_error = { ts, stage, description }` to KV, triggers alert (Layer 4). Green state: writes `canary:state = \"GREEN\"` + `canary:last_check = ts`.\n\n**Why 5 minutes:** Deepgram's own status page shows incidents resolving in 15-30 min windows. 5-min canary catches it within one check. Students typically tap the mic within 2-3 minutes of opening the portal — a 5-min canary means at most one student hits a broken session before the alert fires.\n\n**Cost:** CF Workers cron trigger — free tier covers unlimited triggers. The WS connection is 1 Deepgram credit per canary run. Acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 2 — POST-DEPLOY VERIFY + AUTO-ROLLBACK\n\n**The failure it prevents:** Currently we deploy and assume prod is healthy. A bad deploy can sit broken for an entire student session before anyone notices.\n\n**What it does:** Immediately after every `wrangler deploy`, a script:\n1. Waits 10s for CF propagation\n2. Runs `preflight-ws.mjs` against the just-deployed prod URL (same Gates 2-4)\n3. If all green → deployment confirmed, log deploy version to KV as `deploy:last_good`\n4. If red → **immediately runs `wrangler rollback`** → alerts operator → halts\n\n**Hard rule written into deploy procedure:** A `wrangler deploy` without the post-verify step is a protocol violation. The rollback window is ~60s. A broken deploy self-heals before the first student session after the deploy.\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 3 — STRUCTURED LOGGING (replace console.error with durable signal)\n\n**The failure it prevents:** Every `catch` in the voice path today logs to `console.error`. That evaporates. No trail. No diff between \"one student had a blip\" and \"every student is broken.\"\n\n**Architecture:** A single `logVoiceEvent(env, event)` helper in `src/index.js`:\n\n```\nevent shape: {\n  ts:        epoch ms\n  version:   deploy version (git sha or uuid injected at deploy time)\n  studentId: anonymised (hash, not raw ID)\n  stage:     \"token_fetch\" | \"ws_auth\" | \"settings\" | \"audio\" | \"session_end\"\n  ok:        boolean\n  error:     string | null\n  latency_ms: number\n}\n```\n\n**Sink options (pick one, in order of complexity):**\n- `NET_PET_KV.put(\"log:voice:\" + ts, JSON.stringify(event), { expirationTtl: 604800 })` — 7-day ring buffer in KV. Zero infra. Queryable via `/api/admin/logs`. Sufficient for current scale (3 active students).\n- Logpush to R2 — better for high volume, overkill now.\n- Worker Analytics Engine — Cloudflare native, free, queryable via GraphQL. Best long-term option.\n\n**What gets logged:**\n- Every `/api/deepgram-token` call: studentId hash, latency, ok/error\n- Every circuit breaker state change: open → closed, closed → open, why\n- Every canary run result: stage reached, latency, error description\n- Every post-deploy verify result\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 4 — ALERTING (one real channel, fires on canary red + post-deploy red)\n\n**What it does NOT do:** Email (slow, spam-filtered). Slack webhook (extra setup). Dashboard (no one watches dashboards).\n\n**What it does:** Telegram bot message to operator. Single POST to `https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage`. Arrives on Michael's phone in under 2 seconds. Message format:\n\n```\n🔴 OBI CANARY RED — [stage] failed\nError: [Deepgram description]\nStudents affected: YES (canary fires before next session)\nDeploy version: [version]\nTime: [ts]\nCheck: status.deepgram.com + wrangler tail\n```\n\n**Triggers:**\n- Canary red (any stage)\n- Post-deploy verify red → includes rollback confirmation\n- Circuit breaker opened under student load (not canary)\n- KV error rate > 0 under student load\n\n**Setup required:** One Telegram bot (BotFather, 2 min), one env secret `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`. Already using CF secrets infra — no new system.\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 5 — GRACEFUL DEGRADATION (students get something, not silence)\n\n**The failure it prevents:** When Deepgram is down or canary is RED, a student taps the mic and hears nothing. No message. No explanation. Just silence and confusion.\n\n**What OBI does today when voice breaks:** `onAgentDrop` fires → mic button hidden → network fallback banner shown → text input appears. This is correct for transient network issues but gives no explanation.\n\n**What it should do when the canary is RED:**\n- `/api/deepgram-token` checks `canary:state` in KV before doing anything\n- If RED: returns `{ error: \"voice_unavailable\", message: \"OBI's voice is having a moment — try text chat for now\", retryAfter: 300 }`\n- Portal shows a human-friendly banner: *\"OBI is resting — tap to chat by text instead\"*\n- Text input mode activates automatically (already built in `chat.js`)\n- Student is not left staring at a broken mic with zero feedback\n\n**Cost of this:** 1 KV read (< 1ms) added to the token handler. Returns 503 with a message instead of silent failure. Canary already writes `canary:state` — this just reads it.\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 6 — KV PERFORMANCE FIX (F1 finding — real measured problem)\n\n**The evidence:** Load test from Run 101: 10 concurrent requests, 5s burst → avg **1010ms** latency, **p99 1469ms**, **1 of 44 requests returned 500**. Root cause: every `/api/deepgram-token` call does 8 parallel KV reads + builds the full agent prompt synchronously, every time, for every token request.\n\n**What makes this a real student problem:** Vietnamese students are on mobile networks. 1s token fetch + 200ms WS open + 400ms SettingsApplied = 1.6s before OBI says the first word. On a slow 4G connection this is 3-4s. Students hear silence and tap again. Double connection, chaos.\n\n**Fix architecture:**\n\n```\nFAST PATH: student has cached profile (most sessions)\n  - KV get: student_profile + lang + vocab (3 reads, 50ms)\n  - Skip: session_history, srs_data, memory, phonics (these are for prompt enrichment only)\n  - Return token + base settings in < 200ms\n\nENRICHED PATH: fire-and-forget after token returned\n  - Fetch session_history + srs_data + memory async\n  - Write enriched prompt to KV as \"prompt_cache:{studentId}:{mode}\" with 5min TTL\n  - Next fast-path call reads prompt from cache instead of rebuilding\n\nRESULT: first session of the day = 200ms (fast path)\n         subsequent sessions = < 100ms (cache hit)\n         prompt freshness = 5min max staleness (acceptable — session history doesn't change mid-session)\n```\n\n**What this does NOT touch:** voice brain lock, settings structure, Deepgram WS flow. Pure KV read optimization.\n\n---\n\n## LAYER 7 — /api/health/voice ENDPOINT (one-curl diagnosis)\n\n**The failure it prevents:** Currently diagnosing a broken OBI means reading KV manually, checking CF logs, running preflight-ws.mjs. Takes 5+ minutes.\n\n**What it does:** A single authenticated GET returns the complete voice health picture in one JSON response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ok\": true,\n  \"canary\": {\n    \"state\": \"GREEN\",\n    \"last_check\": \"2026-06-08T09:00:00Z\",\n    \"last_error\": null\n  },\n  \"circuit_breaker\": {\n    \"state\": \"closed\"\n  },\n  \"deploy\": {\n    \"version\": \"b2341008\",\n    \"last_good_deploy\": \"2026-06-08T08:55:00Z\"\n  },\n  \"kv_latency_ms\": 45,\n  \"deepgram_key_alive\": true\n}\n```\n\n**Auth:** requires `X-Admin-Key` header matching a CF secret. If you see \"Degraded Performance\", you do not know which product is affected. The canary tells you precisely which stage fails.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 2 — POST-DEPLOY VERIFY + AUTO-ROLLBACK\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Wrangler docs — `wrangler rollback` (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/#rollback)**\n- `wrangler rollback [deployment-id]` reverts to a specific prior deployment. With no deployment ID, it reverts to the immediately prior version.\n- Deployments are immutable in CF. The prior version is always available for rollback — it was not deleted on deploy.\n- Rollback propagates globally in 15-30s. The old code is live before the next HTTP request completes. This is why the 60s window is safe: 10s wait + 30s post-verify window + 15s rollback propagation = well under 60s.\n- `wrangler deployments list` shows the last 10 deployments with SHA, timestamp, and deployment ID. Save the current deployment ID to KV before deploying so the rollback script always has the exact target.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare blog — \"Zero-downtime deploys with Workers\" (blog.cloudflare.com, 2024)**\n- CF Workers use atomic deployment: the new version handles 100% of traffic the instant propagation completes. There is no gradual rollout unless you explicitly configure a deployment strategy. This means a bad deploy hits all students simultaneously with no warning window.\n- Mitigation: deploy to `net-pet-ai-dev` first (this is already the firewall rule), run post-verify there, then promote to prod. The post-deploy verify on prod catches anything that dev missed due to KV state differences.\n\n**Source: wrangler versions (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/versions-and-deployments)**\n- As of CF Workers Versions API (2024): every upload creates a \"Version\" with a unique ID. A \"Deployment\" points to a Version. `wrangler rollback` creates a new Deployment pointing to the previous Version — it does NOT mutate the Version itself. This means the rollback is auditable and reversible.\n- `wrangler versions list` shows all versions, not just deployments. Useful for bisecting which deploy introduced a bug.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 3 — STRUCTURED LOGGING\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Analytics Engine — official docs (developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine)**\n- Analytics Engine is the best long-term sink. It is write-only from Workers, queryable via GraphQL or the CF dashboard. It is free at current OB-1 scale (3 students). Data is retained for 31 days by default.\n- Write API: `env.MY_AE_DATASET.writeDataPoint({ blobs: [...], doubles: [...], indexes: [...] })`. Max 20 blobs, 20 doubles, 1 index per write. This is sufficient for voice event shape.\n- Caveat: Analytics Engine is eventually consistent. It is NOT suitable for circuit-breaker state reads. Use KV for anything that must be read back immediately (canary state, circuit state). Use AE only as the durable log sink.\n- The `wrangler tail` command already streams logs from production Workers in real time. For early stages, `wrangler tail --format=json | jq 'select(.logs[].message | test(\"ERROR\"))'` is sufficient before AE is wired up.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare KV documentation — TTL and expiration (developers.cloudflare.com/kv/api/write-key-value-pairs)**\n- `expirationTtl` in seconds. The minimum allowed TTL is 60 seconds. Setting `expirationTtl: 604800` (7 days) creates a rolling 7-day log window in KV.\n- KV reads are eventually consistent (15s global propagation). For a ring-buffer log, this is fine — we're reading logs after-the-fact, not doing real-time coordination.\n- KV keys are sorted lexicographically. Using `\"log:voice:\" + ts` with epoch milliseconds gives natural time ordering when listing via `KV.list({ prefix: \"log:voice:\" })`.\n- KV `list` has a 1000-key limit per call. At current scale (3 students, ~10 sessions/day each), 7 days of logs = ~210 entries. Well under the limit.\n\n**Source: GDPR/PDPA anonymization — Vietnamese data protection context**\n- Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Decree (Decree 13/2023) requires that personal data (student names, IDs) not be logged in cleartext. Hashing the student ID before logging (SHA-256, first 8 chars) satisfies the pseudonymization requirement.\n- The hash must be consistent per student ID (same input = same hash) so logs can be correlated across sessions without storing the raw ID. Node.js `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(studentId).digest('hex').slice(0,8)` gives this.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 4 — TELEGRAM ALERTING\n\n**Source: Telegram Bot API official docs (core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage)**\n- Endpoint: `POST https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage`\n- Required fields: `chat_id` (your personal Telegram ID or group ID), `text`\n- Rate limit: 30 messages/second to different chats, 1 message/second to the same chat. The canary fires at most once per 5 minutes — zero concern.\n- `parse_mode: \"HTML\"` or `\"MarkdownV2\"` allows bold/monospace formatting in alerts. Never appears in `wrangler.toml` or source code.\n- Secrets are environment-specific. Set separately for dev and prod environments. The canary on dev should alert to a different Telegram chat (or not alert at all) to avoid noise.\n\n**Source: ops alerting patterns — community (community.cloudflare.com and various CF Workers showcase posts)**\n- The most common mistake: alerting on every canary check instead of only on state transitions. Implement a \"RED → GREEN\" and \"GREEN → RED\" transition check in KV. If the previous state was already RED and the new check is also RED, suppress the alert — it was already sent. Only send again when state changes. This prevents alert storms during extended Deepgram outages.\n- Pattern: `KV.put(\"canary:state\", \"RED\", { expirationTtl: 3600 })` + `KV.put(\"canary:alerted_at\", ts)`. On next canary run: read `canary:state` first. If already RED and `alerted_at` is within 30 min, skip alert. Otherwise re-alert (catches \"still down\" reminder) and update `alerted_at`.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 5 — GRACEFUL DEGRADATION\n\n**Source: Martin Fowler — \"Circuit Breaker\" pattern (martinfowler.com/bliki/CircuitBreaker.html)**\n- The canary-state check in Layer 5 is a read-only circuit breaker: \"if the last N checks failed, stop sending real traffic into the dependency and fall back.\" This is the canonical circuit breaker pattern applied at the token-grant layer.\n- The key distinction: the circuit is opened by the canary (a background probe), not by real student traffic. This means students never generate the probe failures — the canary absorbs them. The circuit opens before the first student is impacted.\n- Recovery: the canary automatically closes the circuit when SettingsApplied + audio succeed again. No manual intervention.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers KV conditional response pattern (community posts)**\n- The `canary:state` read adds ~1ms to the token handler (KV read from same PoP). On a 1010ms p99 baseline (Run 101 F1 finding), this is noise.\n- HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 300` header is the RFC-correct response for a temporarily unavailable service. Browsers and fetch() clients respect this header. The portal's existing retry logic (if any) will honor it automatically.\n\n**Source: Deepgram Voice Agent text fallback (developers.deepgram.com/docs/voice-agent-overview)**\n- Deepgram's own docs acknowledge that network quality affects Voice Agent performance. They recommend implementing a text fallback in production apps. This validates our Layer 5 design.\n- The `onAgentDrop` handler already exists in magic-chat.js (built in a prior run). Layer 5 is a forward-path gate (`canary:state` → 503 → portal shows banner) rather than a reactive recovery. Both mechanisms should coexist.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 6 — KV PERFORMANCE FIX\n\n**Source: Cloudflare KV performance characteristics — official docs + blog (developers.cloudflare.com/kv/reference/how-kv-works)**\n- KV reads served from the edge PoP cache hit in ~1ms. KV reads that miss the PoP cache (cold reads) fetch from the nearest storage region in ~30-50ms for reads, up to ~200ms for writes. The 8 parallel reads on the token handler are all cold on the first request after a deployment or after the cache expires (60s default for read cache).\n- Cache TTL on reads: CF caches KV reads at the edge for 60 seconds by default. After 60s, the next read is a cold fetch. Setting `{ cacheTtl: 300 }` on KV reads extends the edge cache to 5 minutes, eliminating cold read latency for 99% of calls at current student volume (3 students, sessions spaced > 5 min apart).\n- `cacheTtl` is a read hint, not a write guarantee. It does NOT affect consistency. This is safe to use on student profile data since profiles don't change mid-session.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare blog — \"How KV works\" (blog.cloudflare.com, 2023)**\n- Writes always bypass the cache. After writing a student profile update (e.g., SRS data after a session), the next read within 60s still returns the pre-update cached value. For our fast path (read-heavy, write after session end), this is acceptable. The prompt is slightly stale during the session — this is the intended behavior.\n- CF KV is optimized for read-heavy workloads. The Workers team explicitly recommends caching frequently-read keys like configuration and user profile data at the application layer (in addition to KV's built-in cache). The `prompt_cache:{studentId}` approach in Layer 6 is aligned with CF's own guidance.\n\n**Source: Run 101 load test (autocannon, 10 connections / 5s, human-measured)**\n- Baseline: p99 1469ms, avg 1010ms, 1 of 44 requests returned 500 under 10-way concurrency\n- The 500 is almost certainly a KV consistency error: under concurrent load, two requests race on the `circuit:deepgram:state` read. The `if (env.NET_PET_KV)` guard was added in a prior run but the read/write race under concurrency was not addressed.\n- Fix: make circuit breaker reads idempotent by treating a missing key as \"closed\" (already done) AND by never writing to the circuit key on the hot read path — only the canary should write to `circuit:deepgram:state`, not individual token requests.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 7 — /api/health/voice\n\n**Source: IETF Health Check Response Format RFC — draft-inadarei-api-health-check (tools.ietf.org/html/draft-inadarei-api-health-check)**\n- The Internet Draft for health check endpoints defines a standard JSON format: `{ \"status\": \"pass\"|\"fail\"|\"warn\", \"version\": \"...\", \"checks\": { \"component\": [{ \"status\": \"pass\", \"time\": \"...\", \"output\": \"...\" }] } }`. Adopting this format makes the endpoint compatible with any standard health check tool (uptime monitors, k8s probes, etc.).\n- The `status` values are \"pass\" (healthy), \"fail\" (unhealthy), \"warn\" (degraded but serving). For OBI: canary GREEN = pass, canary RED = warn (students get text fallback), circuit OPEN = fail.\n- Content-Type: `application/health+json` (not `application/json`). Some monitoring tools check this header. Worth setting correctly from the start.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers authentication patterns (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/auth-with-headers)**\n- `X-Admin-Key` header check: `if (request.headers.get(\"X-Admin-Key\") !== env.ADMIN_KEY) return new Response(\"Unauthorized\", { status: 401 })`. Simple and sufficient for a diagnostic endpoint.\n- Do NOT expose the health endpoint without auth. It leaks deployment version, KV state keys, and circuit breaker status — all useful to an attacker probing for windows of degraded availability.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects vs KV for health state (community discussion, 2024)**\n- Several CF community posts note that reading health state from KV (eventual consistency, 60s cache) can return stale GREEN when the canary just wrote RED. For a diagnostic endpoint used by a human operator (not automated failover), 60s stale data is acceptable. For automated rollback triggers, use Durable Objects instead (strong consistency). This means a bad deploy hits all students simultaneously with no warning window.\n- Mitigation: deploy to `net-pet-ai-dev` first (this is already the firewall rule), run post-verify there, then promote to prod. The post-deploy verify on prod catches anything that dev missed due to KV state differences.\n\n**Source: wrangler versions (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/versions-and-deployments)**\n- As of CF Workers Versions API (2024): every upload creates a \"Version\" with a unique ID. A \"Deployment\" points to a Version. `wrangler rollback` creates a new Deployment pointing to the previous Version — it does NOT mutate the Version itself. This means the rollback is auditable and reversible.\n- `wrangler versions list` shows all versions, not just deployments. Useful for bisecting which deploy introduced a bug.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 3 — STRUCTURED LOGGING\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Analytics Engine — official docs (developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine)**\n- Analytics Engine is the best long-term sink. It is write-only from Workers, queryable via GraphQL or the CF dashboard. It is free at current OB-1 scale (3 students). Data is retained for 31 days by default.\n- Write API: `env.MY_AE_DATASET.writeDataPoint({ blobs: [...], doubles: [...], indexes: [...] })`. Max 20 blobs, 20 doubles, 1 index per write. This is sufficient for voice event shape.\n- Caveat: Analytics Engine is eventually consistent. It is NOT suitable for circuit-breaker state reads. Use KV for anything that must be read back immediately (canary state, circuit state). Use AE only as the durable log sink.\n- The `wrangler tail` command already streams logs from production Workers in real time. For early stages, `wrangler tail --format=json | jq 'select(.logs[].message | test(\"ERROR\"))'` is sufficient before AE is wired up.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare KV documentation — TTL and expiration (developers.cloudflare.com/kv/api/write-key-value-pairs)**\n- `expirationTtl` in seconds. The minimum allowed TTL is 60 seconds. Setting `expirationTtl: 604800` (7 days) creates a rolling 7-day log window in KV.\n- KV reads are eventually consistent (15s global propagation). For a ring-buffer log, this is fine — we're reading logs after-the-fact, not doing real-time coordination.\n- KV keys are sorted lexicographically. Using `\"log:voice:\" + ts` with epoch milliseconds gives natural time ordering when listing via `KV.list({ prefix: \"log:voice:\" })`.\n- KV `list` has a 1000-key limit per call. At current scale (3 students, ~10 sessions/day each), 7 days of logs = ~210 entries. Well under the limit.\n\n**Source: GDPR/PDPA anonymization — Vietnamese data protection context**\n- Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Decree (Decree 13/2023) requires that personal data (student names, IDs) not be logged in cleartext. Hashing the student ID before logging (SHA-256, first 8 chars) satisfies the pseudonymization requirement.\n- The hash must be consistent per student ID (same input = same hash) so logs can be correlated across sessions without storing the raw ID. Node.js `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(studentId).digest('hex').slice(0,8)` gives this.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 4 — TELEGRAM ALERTING\n\n**Source: Telegram Bot API official docs (core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage)**\n- Endpoint: `POST https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage`\n- Required fields: `chat_id` (your personal Telegram ID or group ID), `text`\n- Rate limit: 30 messages/second to different chats, 1 message/second to the same chat. The canary fires at most once per 5 minutes — zero concern.\n- `parse_mode: \"HTML\"` or `\"MarkdownV2\"` allows bold/monospace formatting in alerts. Example: `<b>🔴 OBI CANARY RED</b>\\n<code>stage: SettingsApplied timeout</code>`\n- To get your personal `chat_id`: send any message to your bot, then `GET https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/getUpdates` — the `message.chat.id` field is your ID.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers environment secrets (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/secrets)**\n- `wrangler secret put TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` — stores encrypted at rest, injected at runtime as `env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. Never appears in `wrangler.toml` or source code.\n- Secrets are environment-specific. Set separately for dev and prod environments. The canary on dev should alert to a different Telegram chat (or not alert at all) to avoid noise.\n\n**Source: ops alerting patterns — community (community.cloudflare.com and various CF Workers showcase posts)**\n- The most common mistake: alerting on every canary check instead of only on state transitions. Implement a \"RED → GREEN\" and \"GREEN → RED\" transition check in KV. If the previous state was already RED and the new check is also RED, suppress the alert — it was already sent. Only send again when state changes. This prevents alert storms during extended Deepgram outages.\n- Pattern: `KV.put(\"canary:state\", \"RED\", { expirationTtl: 3600 })` + `KV.put(\"canary:alerted_at\", ts)`. On next canary run: read `canary:state` first. If already RED and `alerted_at` is within 30 min, skip alert. Otherwise re-alert (catches \"still down\" reminder) and update `alerted_at`.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 5 — GRACEFUL DEGRADATION\n\n**Source: Martin Fowler — \"Circuit Breaker\" pattern (martinfowler.com/bliki/CircuitBreaker.html)**\n- The canary-state check in Layer 5 is a read-only circuit breaker: \"if the last N checks failed, stop sending real traffic into the dependency and fall back.\" This is the canonical circuit breaker pattern applied at the token-grant layer.\n- The key distinction: the circuit is opened by the canary (a background probe), not by real student traffic. This means students never generate the probe failures — the canary absorbs them. The circuit opens before the first student is impacted.\n- Recovery: the canary automatically closes the circuit when SettingsApplied + audio succeed again. No manual intervention.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers KV conditional response pattern (community posts)**\n- The `canary:state` read adds ~1ms to the token handler (KV read from same PoP). On a 1010ms p99 baseline (Run 101 F1 finding), this is noise.\n- HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 300` header is the RFC-correct response for a temporarily unavailable service. Browsers and fetch() clients respect this header. The portal's existing retry logic (if any) will honor it automatically.\n\n**Source: Deepgram Voice Agent text fallback (developers.deepgram.com/docs/voice-agent-overview)**\n- Deepgram's own docs acknowledge that network quality affects Voice Agent performance. They recommend implementing a text fallback in production apps. This validates our Layer 5 design.\n- The `onAgentDrop` handler already exists in magic-chat.js (built in a prior run). Layer 5 is a forward-path gate (`canary:state` → 503 → portal shows banner) rather than a reactive recovery. Both mechanisms should coexist.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 6 — KV PERFORMANCE FIX\n\n**Source: Cloudflare KV performance characteristics — official docs + blog (developers.cloudflare.com/kv/reference/how-kv-works)**\n- KV reads served from the edge PoP cache hit in ~1ms. KV reads that miss the PoP cache (cold reads) fetch from the nearest storage region in ~30-50ms for reads, up to ~200ms for writes. The 8 parallel reads on the token handler are all cold on the first request after a deployment or after the cache expires (60s default for read cache).\n- Cache TTL on reads: CF caches KV reads at the edge for 60 seconds by default. After 60s, the next read is a cold fetch. Setting `{ cacheTtl: 300 }` on KV reads extends the edge cache to 5 minutes, eliminating cold read latency for 99% of calls at current student volume (3 students, sessions spaced > 5 min apart).\n- `cacheTtl` is a read hint, not a write guarantee. It does NOT affect consistency. This is safe to use on student profile data since profiles don't change mid-session.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare blog — \"How KV works\" (blog.cloudflare.com, 2023)**\n- Writes always bypass the cache. After writing a student profile update (e.g., SRS data after a session), the next read within 60s still returns the pre-update cached value. For our fast path (read-heavy, write after session end), this is acceptable. The prompt is slightly stale during the session — this is the intended behavior.\n- CF KV is optimized for read-heavy workloads. The Workers team explicitly recommends caching frequently-read keys like configuration and user profile data at the application layer (in addition to KV's built-in cache). The `prompt_cache:{studentId}` approach in Layer 6 is aligned with CF's own guidance.\n\n**Source: Run 101 load test (autocannon, 10 connections / 5s, human-measured)**\n- Baseline: p99 1469ms, avg 1010ms, 1 of 44 requests returned 500 under 10-way concurrency\n- The 500 is almost certainly a KV consistency error: under concurrent load, two requests race on the `circuit:deepgram:state` read. The `if (env.NET_PET_KV)` guard was added in a prior run but the read/write race under concurrency was not addressed.\n- Fix: make circuit breaker reads idempotent by treating a missing key as \"closed\" (already done) AND by never writing to the circuit key on the hot read path — only the canary should write to `circuit:deepgram:state`, not individual token requests.\n\n---\n\n### LAYER 7 — /api/health/voice\n\n**Source: IETF Health Check Response Format RFC — draft-inadarei-api-health-check (tools.ietf.org/html/draft-inadarei-api-health-check)**\n- The Internet Draft for health check endpoints defines a standard JSON format: `{ \"status\": \"pass\"|\"fail\"|\"warn\", \"version\": \"...\", \"checks\": { \"component\": [{ \"status\": \"pass\", \"time\": \"...\", \"output\": \"...\" }] } }`. Adopting this format makes the endpoint compatible with any standard health check tool (uptime monitors, k8s probes, etc.).\n- The `status` values are \"pass\" (healthy), \"fail\" (unhealthy), \"warn\" (degraded but serving). For OBI: canary GREEN = pass, canary RED = warn (students get text fallback), circuit OPEN = fail.\n- Content-Type: `application/health+json` (not `application/json`). Some monitoring tools check this header. Worth setting correctly from the start.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers authentication patterns (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/auth-with-headers)**\n- `X-Admin-Key` header check: `if (request.headers.get(\"X-Admin-Key\") !== env.ADMIN_KEY) return new Response(\"Unauthorized\", { status: 401 })`. Simple and sufficient for a diagnostic endpoint.\n- Do NOT expose the health endpoint without auth. It leaks deployment version, KV state keys, and circuit breaker status — all useful to an attacker probing for windows of degraded availability.\n\n**Source: Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects vs KV for health state (community discussion, 2024)**\n- Several CF community posts note that reading health state from KV (eventual consistency, 60s cache) can return stale GREEN when the canary just wrote RED. For a diagnostic endpoint used by a human operator (not automated failover), 60s stale data is acceptable. For automated rollback triggers, use Durable Objects instead (strong consistency). Layer 2 rollback uses `wrangler rollback` triggered by the post-deploy script — not by the health endpoint — so KV is fine here.\n\n---\n\n## WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER (belongs in separate blueprints)","originalFile":"# /netpet-observability — OBI Production Observability + Resilience Blueprint\n\n**What this covers:** Everything that happens BETWEEN deploys. Node.js `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(studentId).digest('hex').slice(0,8)` gives this.","+","+---","+","+### LAYER 4 — TELEGRAM ALERTING","+","+**Source: Telegram Bot API official docs (core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage)**","+- Endpoint: `POST https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/sendMessage`","+- Required fields: `chat_id` (your personal Telegram ID or group ID), `text`","+- Rate limit: 30 messages/second to different chats, 1 message/second to the same chat. The canary fires at most once per 5 minutes — zero concern.","+- `parse_mode: \"HTML\"` or `\"MarkdownV2\"` allows bold/monospace formatting in alerts. Example: `<b>🔴 OBI CANARY RED</b>\\n<code>stage: SettingsApplied timeout</code>`","+- To get your personal `chat_id`: send any message to your bot, then `GET https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}/getUpdates` — the `message.chat.id` field is your ID.","+","+**Source: Cloudflare Workers environment secrets (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/secrets)**","+- `wrangler secret put TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` — stores encrypted at rest, injected at runtime as `env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. Never appears in `wrangler.toml` or source code.","+- Secrets are environment-specific. Set separately for dev and prod environments. The canary on dev should alert to a different Telegram chat (or not alert at all) to avoid noise.","+","+**Source: ops alerting patterns — community (community.cloudflare.com and various CF Workers showcase posts)**","+- The most common mistake: alerting on every canary check instead of only on state transitions. Implement a \"RED → GREEN\" and \"GREEN → RED\" transition check in KV. If the previous state was already RED and the new check is also RED, suppress the alert — it was already sent. Only send again when state changes. This prevents alert storms during extended Deepgram outages.","+- Pattern: `KV.put(\"canary:state\", \"RED\", { expirationTtl: 3600 })` + `KV.put(\"canary:alerted_at\", ts)`. On next canary run: read `canary:state` first. If already RED and `alerted_at` is within 30 min, skip alert. Otherwise re-alert (catches \"still down\" reminder) and update `alerted_at`.","+","+---","+","+### LAYER 5 — GRACEFUL DEGRADATION","+","+**Source: Martin Fowler — \"Circuit Breaker\" pattern (martinfowler.com/bliki/CircuitBreaker.html)**","+- The canary-state check in Layer 5 is a read-only circuit breaker: \"if the last N checks failed, stop sending real traffic into the dependency and fall back.\" This is the canonical circuit breaker pattern applied at the token-grant layer.","+- The key distinction: the circuit is opened by the canary (a background probe), not by real student traffic. This means students never generate the probe failures — the canary absorbs them. The circuit opens before the first student is impacted.","+- Recovery: the canary automatically closes the circuit when SettingsApplied + audio succeed again. No manual intervention.","+","+**Source: Cloudflare Workers KV conditional response pattern (community posts)**","+- The `canary:state` read adds ~1ms to the token handler (KV read from same PoP). On a 1010ms p99 baseline (Run 101 F1 finding), this is noise.","+- HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 300` header is the RFC-correct response for a temporarily unavailable service. Browsers and fetch() clients respect this header. The portal's existing retry logic (if any) will honor it automatically.","+","+**Source: Deepgram Voice Agent text fallback (developers.deepgram.com/docs/voice-agent-overview)**","+- Deepgram's own docs acknowledge that network quality affects Voice Agent performance. They recommend implementing a text fallback in production apps. This validates our Layer 5 design.","+- The `onAgentDrop` handler already exists in magic-chat.js (built in a prior run). Layer 5 is a forward-path gate (`canary:state` → 503 → portal shows banner) rather than a reactive recovery. Both mechanisms should coexist.","+","+---","+","+### LAYER 6 — KV PERFORMANCE FIX","+","+**Source: Cloudflare KV performance characteristics — official docs + blog (developers.cloudflare.com/kv/reference/how-kv-works)**","+- KV reads served from the edge PoP cache hit in ~1ms. KV reads that miss the PoP cache (cold reads) fetch from the nearest storage region in ~30-50ms for reads, up to ~200ms for writes. The 8 parallel reads on the token handler are all cold on the first request after a deployment or after the cache expires (60s default for read cache).","+- Cache TTL on reads: CF caches KV reads at the edge for 60 seconds by default. After 60s, the next read is a cold fetch. Setting `{ cacheTtl: 300 }` on KV reads extends the edge cache to 5 minutes, eliminating cold read latency for 99% of calls at current student volume (3 students, sessions spaced > 5 min apart).","+- `cacheTtl` is a read hint, not a write guarantee. It does NOT affect consistency. This is safe to use on student profile data since profiles don't change mid-session.","+","+**Source: Cloudflare blog — \"How KV works\" (blog.cloudflare.com, 2023)**","+- Writes always bypass the cache. After writing a student profile update (e.g., SRS data after a session), the next read within 60s still returns the pre-update cached value. For our fast path (read-heavy, write after session end), this is acceptable. The prompt is slightly stale during the session — this is the intended behavior.","+- CF KV is optimized for read-heavy workloads. The Workers team explicitly recommends caching frequently-read keys like configuration and user profile data at the application layer (in addition to KV's built-in cache). The `prompt_cache:{studentId}` approach in Layer 6 is aligned with CF's own guidance.","+","+**Source: Run 101 load test (autocannon, 10 connections / 5s, human-measured)**","+- Baseline: p99 1469ms, avg 1010ms, 1 of 44 requests returned 500 under 10-way concurrency","+- The 500 is almost certainly a KV consistency error: under concurrent load, two requests race on the `circuit:deepgram:state` read. The `if (env.NET_PET_KV)` guard was added in a prior run but the read/write race under concurrency was not addressed.","+- Fix: make circuit breaker reads idempotent by treating a missing key as \"closed\" (already done) AND by never writing to the circuit key on the hot read path — only the canary should write to `circuit:deepgram:state`, not individual token requests.","+","+---","+","+### LAYER 7 — /api/health/voice","+","+**Source: IETF Health Check Response Format RFC — draft-inadarei-api-health-check (tools.ietf.org/html/draft-inadarei-api-health-check)**","+- The Internet Draft for health check endpoints defines a standard JSON format: `{ \"status\": \"pass\"|\"fail\"|\"warn\", \"version\": \"...\", \"checks\": { \"component\": [{ \"status\": \"pass\", \"time\": \"...\", \"output\": \"...\" }] } }`. Adopting this format makes the endpoint compatible with any standard health check tool (uptime monitors, k8s probes, etc.).","+- The `status` values are \"pass\" (healthy), \"fail\" (unhealthy), \"warn\" (degraded but serving). For OBI: canary GREEN = pass, canary RED = warn (students get text fallback), circuit OPEN = fail.","+- Content-Type: `application/health+json` (not `application/json`). Some monitoring tools check this header. Worth setting correctly from the start.","+","+**Source: Cloudflare Workers authentication patterns (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/auth-with-headers)**","+- `X-Admin-Key` header check: `if (request.headers.get(\"X-Admin-Key\") !== env.ADMIN_KEY) return new Response(\"Unauthorized\", { status: 401 })`. Simple and sufficient for a diagnostic endpoint.","+- Do NOT expose the health endpoint without auth. It leaks deployment version, KV state keys, and circuit breaker status — all useful to an attacker probing for windows of degraded availability.","+","+**Source: Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects vs KV for health state (community discussion, 2024)**","+- Several CF community posts note that reading health state from KV (eventual consistency, 60s cache) can return stale GREEN when the canary just wrote RED. For a diagnostic endpoint used by a human operator (not automated failover), 60s stale data is acceptable. For automated rollback triggers, use Durable Objects instead (strong consistency). Layer 2 rollback uses `wrangler rollback` triggered by the post-deploy script — not by the health endpoint — so KV is fine here.","+","+---","+"," ## WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER (belongs in separate blueprints)"," "," - Pre-deploy functional gates → `/netpet-preflight.md` (Kilo is on this)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8df9bcd7-9e18-4bde-a5df-092da9300b3a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"d:\\OB-1-CANONICAL","sessionId":"546cc484-6f27-4b01-930e-6c52fe2a30ef","version":"2.1.167","gitBranch":"master","slug":"harmonic-wibbling-crystal"}

\"\"\n$inAssistantBlock = $false\n\nforeach ($line in $lines) {\n    $trimmed = $line.Trim()\n    \n    # Detect role markers (JSONL format)\n    if ($trimmed -match '\"role\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"')       $dnaRecords += [ordered]@{\n                run    = $run\n                seq    = $turnSeq\n                type   = if ($isBlueprint) { \"blueprint\" } else { \"prose\" }\n                chars  = $text.Length\n                text   = $text\n            }\n        }\n        $inAssistantBlock = $true\n        $currentBlock = $trimmed -replace '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent Plain-text path (line ~209): speaker-marker line (\"AGENT:\") is INCLUDED with prefix stripped\n#   Result: same semantic turn produces different character counts depending on which parser path was semantic content.\n$dnaTotalCharsJsonl  = 0\n$dnaTotalCharsPlain  = 0\n$dnaJsonlRecords     = ($dnaRecords | Where-Object { $_.text -notmatch '^(AGENT|OB1|ASSISTANT|Agent 99)\\s*[:|>-]' Write-Warning \"STAGE 3 ⚠ DNA_GAP — 0 assistant turns extracted from RRL\"\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## STAGE 4 — LEDGER (MERKLE — DUAL HASH OVER SOUL + DNA)\n\n```powershell\n# --- Helper Functions ---\nfunction Get-Next-LedgerID {\n    param([string]$LedgerDir)\n    $existing = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $LedgerDir -Filter \"HL-*.json\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |\n        ForEach-Object { if (-not $latest) { return $null }\n    $entry = Get-Content $latest.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json\n    return $entry.merkle_hash\n}\nfunction Compute-Sha256 {\n    param([string]$InputString)\n
